$Comment: Ranger Wren, the Emerald Wilds quest giver, standing beside a Kweebec village.
Where: the world named 'default', which is the persistent world players log into, never an
instance - a bare word under Match is an exact name. If your server's main world has another
name, change it here (or override this placement by id from your own pack).
Anchor.Structure attaches the placement to a worldgen spawn marker rather than to fixed
coordinates, so Wren lands in a village the world actually generated instead of an arbitrary
spot. MarkerIds is an exact, case-insensitive allow-list; run /mmonpc structures in game to see
the marker ids a world has actually loaded before authoring one. The allow-list is FAIL-CLOSED:
a typo means Wren simply never appears.
Limits: one per world, and every matching marker is used (SpawnChance 1 means never skipped).
Raise MaxPerWorld to stand one at every matching village instead.
Identity.Role names the NPC role this placement spawns. Wren's look and nameplate live in that
role file (Server/NPC/Roles/Passive/Guide_Wilds.json), which this pack ships, so re-dress her
there rather than here. Point Role at a different role id to stand somebody else at the villages.
This placement authors no Identity.NpcId, so the character IS its role: the pack's quests
name Guide_Wilds as their npcViewId, the dialogue destination below carries it, and a talk step
credits against it. Author an NpcId to make this standing a character of its own that
nothing else answers to.
Press F opens Wren's dialogue. It is authored as a ui_target rather than as Interact.Dialogue
because that form carries the character id into the dialogue, which is what Wren's own
'npcquests:@self' options resolve against and what puts the character's name in the header.
Authoring Interact.Dialogue instead would open the same tree with no identity and those options
would go nowhere. That id is also what the pack's quests bind as their npcViewId.
Name: Guide_Wilds
